66:def concat(
67:    objs,

72:    positions=None,
73:    fill_value=dtypes.NA,

78:    """Concatenate xarray objects along a new or existing dimension.
79:
80:    Parameters
81:    ----------
82:    objs : sequence of Dataset and DataArray
83:        xarray objects to concatenate together. Each object is expected to
84:        consist of variables and coordinates with matching shapes except for
85:        along the concatenated dimension.
86:    dim : Hashable or Variable or DataArray or pandas.Index
87:        Name of the dimension to concatenate along. This can either be a new
88:        dimension name, in which case it is added along axis=0, or an existing
89:        dimension name, in which case the location of the dimension is
90:        unchanged. If dimension is provided as a Variable, DataArray or Index, its name
91:        is used as the dimension to concatenate along and the values are added
92:        as a coordinate.
93:    data_vars : {"minimal", "different", "all"} or list of Hashable, optional
94:        These data variables will be concatenated together:
95:          * "minimal": Only data variables in which the dimension already
96:            appears are included.
97:          * "different": Data variables which are not equal (ignoring
98:            attributes) across all datasets are also concatenated (as well as
99:            all for which dimension already appears). Beware: this option may
100:            load the data payload of data variables into memory if they are not
101:            already loaded.
102:          * "all": All data variables will be concatenated.
103:          * list of dims: The listed data variables will be concatenated, in
104:            addition to the "minimal" data variables.
105:
106:        If objects are DataArrays, data_vars must be "all".
107:    coords : {"minimal", "different", "all"} or list of Hashable, optional
108:        These coordinate variables will be concatenated together:
109:          * "minimal": Only coordinates in which the dimension already appears
110:            are included.
111:          * "different": Coordinates which are not equal (ignoring attributes)
112:            across all datasets are also concatenated (as well as all for which
113:            dimension already appears). Beware: this option may load the data
114:            payload of coordinate variables into memory if they are not already
115:            loaded.
116:          * "all": All coordinate variables will be concatenated, except
117:            those corresponding to other dimensions.
118:          * list of Hashable: The listed coordinate variables will be concatenated,
119:            in addition to the "minimal" coordinates.
120:    compat : {"identical", "equals", "broadcast_equals", "no_conflicts", "override"}, optional
121:        String indicating how to compare non-concatenated variables of the same name for
122:        potential conflicts. This is passed down to merge.
123:
124:        - "broadcast_equals": all values must be equal when variables are
125:          broadcast against each other to ensure common dimensions.
126:        - "equals": all values and dimensions must be the same.
127:        - "identical": all values, dimensions and attributes must be the
128:          same.
129:        - "no_conflicts": only values which are not null in both datasets
130:          must be equal. The returned dataset then contains the combination
131:          of all non-null values.
132:        - "override": skip comparing and pick variable from first dataset
133:    positions : None or list of integer arrays, optional
134:        List of integer arrays which specifies the integer positions to which
135:        to assign each dataset along the concatenated dimension. If not
136:        supplied, objects are concatenated in the provided order.
137:    fill_value : scalar or dict-like, optional
138:        Value to use for newly missing values. If a dict-like, maps
139:        variable names to fill values. Use a data array's name to
140:        refer to its values.
141:    join : {"outer", "inner", "left", "right", "exact"}, optional
142:        String indicating how to combine differing indexes
143:        (excluding dim) in objects
144:
145:        - "outer": use the union of object indexes
146:        - "inner": use the intersection of object indexes
147:        - "left": use indexes from the first object with each dimension
148:        - "right": use indexes from the last object with each dimension
149:        - "exact": instead of aligning, raise `ValueError` when indexes to be
150:          aligned are not equal
151:        - "override": if indexes are of same size, rewrite indexes to be
152:          those of the first object with that dimension. Indexes for the same
153:          dimension must have the same size in all objects.
154:    combine_attrs : {"drop", "identical", "no_conflicts", "drop_conflicts", \
155:                     "override"} or callable, default: "override"
156:        A callable or a string indicating how to combine attrs of the objects being
157:        merged:
158:
159:        - "drop": empty attrs on returned Dataset.
160:        - "identical": all attrs must be the same on every object.
161:        - "no_conflicts": attrs from all objects are combined, any that have
162:          the same name must also have the same value.
163:        - "drop_conflicts": attrs from all objects are combined, any that have
164:          the same name but different values are dropped.
165:        - "override": skip comparing and copy attrs from the first dataset to
166:          the result.
167:
168:        If a callable, it must expect a sequence of ``attrs`` dicts and a context object
169:        as its only parameters.
170:    create_index_for_new_dim : bool, default: True
171:        Whether to create a new ``PandasIndex`` object when the objects being concatenated contain scalar variables named ``dim``.
172:
173:    Returns
174:    -------
175:    concatenated : type of objs
176:
177:    See also
178:    --------
179:    merge
180:
181:    Examples
182:    --------
183:    >>> da = xr.DataArray(

193:

195:    <xarray.DataArray (x: 2, y: 3)> Size: 48B
196:    array([[0, 1, 2],
197:           [3, 4, 5]])
198:    Coordinates:
199:      * x        (x) <U1 8B 'a' 'b'
200:      * y        (y) int64 24B 10 20 30
201:
202:    >>> xr.concat([da.isel(x=0), da.isel(x=1)], "x")
203:    <xarray.DataArray (x: 2, y: 3)> Size: 48B
204:    array([[0, 1, 2],
205:           [3, 4, 5]])
206:    Coordinates:
207:      * x        (x) <U1 8B 'a' 'b'
208:      * y        (y) int64 24B 10 20 30
209:
210:    >>> xr.concat([da.isel(x=0), da.isel(x=1)], "new_dim")
211:    <xarray.DataArray (new_dim: 2, y: 3)> Size: 48B
212:    array([[0, 1, 2],
213:           [3, 4, 5]])
214:    Coordinates:
215:        x        (new_dim) <U1 8B 'a' 'b'
216:      * y        (y) int64 24B 10 20 30
217:    Dimensions without coordinates: new_dim
218:
219:    >>> xr.concat([da.isel(x=0), da.isel(x=1)], pd.Index([-90, -100], name="new_dim"))

297:    dim_or_data: Hashable | Any,

299:    """Infer the dimension name and 1d index / coordinate variable (if appropriate)
300:    for concatenating along the new dimension.
301:
302:    """

304:
305:    dim: Hashable | None
306:
307:    if utils.hashable(dim_or_data):
308:        dim = dim_or_data
309:        index = None
310:    else:
311:        if not isinstance(dim_or_data, DataArray | Variable):
312:            dim = getattr(dim_or_data, "name", None)
313:            if dim is None:
314:                dim = "concat_dim"
315:        else:
316:            (dim,) = dim_or_data.dims
317:        coord_dtype = getattr(dim_or_data, "dtype", None)
318:        index = PandasIndex(dim_or_data, dim, coord_dtype=coord_dtype)

323:def _calc_concat_over(datasets, dim, dim_names, data_vars: T_DataVars, coords, compat):
324:    """
325:    Determine which dataset variables need to be concatenated in the result,
326:    """
327:    # Return values
328:    concat_over = set()
329:    equals = {}
330:
331:    if dim in dim_names:
332:        concat_over_existing_dim = True
333:        concat_over.add(dim)
334:    else:
335:        concat_over_existing_dim = False
336:
337:    concat_dim_lengths = []
338:    for ds in datasets:
339:        if concat_over_existing_dim:
340:            if dim not in ds.dims:
341:                if dim in ds:
342:                    ds = ds.set_coords(dim)
343:        concat_over.update(k for k, v in ds.variables.items() if dim in v.dims)
344:        concat_dim_lengths.append(ds.sizes.get(dim, 1))
345:
346:    def process_subset_opt(opt, subset):
347:        if isinstance(opt, str):
348:            if opt == "different":
349:                if compat == "override":
350:                    raise ValueError(
351:                        f"Cannot specify both {subset}='different' and compat='override'."
352:                    )
353:                # all nonindexes that are not the same in each dataset
354:                for k in getattr(datasets[0], subset):
355:                    if k not in concat_over:
356:                        equals[k] = None
357:
358:                        variables = [
359:                            ds.variables[k] for ds in datasets if k in ds.variables
360:                        ]
361:
362:                        if len(variables) == 1:
363:                            # coords="different" doesn't make sense when only one object
364:                            # contains a particular variable.
365:                            break
366:                        elif len(variables) != len(datasets) and opt == "different":
367:                            raise ValueError(
368:                                f"{k!r} not present in all datasets and coords='different'. "
369:                                f"Either add {k!r} to datasets where it is missing or "
370:                                "specify coords='minimal'."
371:                            )
372:
373:                        # first check without comparing values i.e. no computes
374:                        for var in variables[1:]:
375:                            equals[k] = getattr(variables[0], compat)(
376:                                var, equiv=lazy_array_equiv
377:                            )
378:                            if equals[k] is not True:
379:                                # exit early if we know these are not equal or that
380:                                # equality cannot be determined i.e. one or all of
381:                                # the variables wraps a numpy array
382:                                break
383:
384:                        if equals[k] is False:
385:                            concat_over.add(k)
386:
387:                        elif equals[k] is None:
388:                            # Compare the variable of all datasets vs. the one
389:                            # of the first dataset. Perform the minimum amount of
390:                            # loads in order to avoid multiple loads from disk
391:                            # while keeping the RAM footprint low.
392:                            v_lhs = datasets[0].variables[k].load()
393:                            # We'll need to know later on if variables are equal.
394:                            computed = []
395:                            for ds_rhs in datasets[1:]:
396:                                v_rhs = ds_rhs.variables[k].compute()
397:                                computed.append(v_rhs)
398:                                if not getattr(v_lhs, compat)(v_rhs):
399:                                    concat_over.add(k)
400:                                    equals[k] = False
401:                                    # computed variables are not to be re-computed
402:                                    # again in the future
403:                                    for ds, v in zip(
404:                                        datasets[1:], computed, strict=False
405:                                    ):
406:                                        ds.variables[k].data = v.data
407:                                    break
408:                            else:
409:                                equals[k] = True

411:            elif opt == "all":

413:                    set().union(

415:                    )

444:# determine dimensional coordinate names and a dict mapping name to DataArray
445:def _parse_datasets(
446:    datasets: list[T_Dataset],
447:) -> tuple[
448:    dict[Hashable, Variable],
449:    dict[Hashable, int],
450:    set[Hashable],
451:    set[Hashable],
452:    list[Hashable],
453:]:
454:    dims: set[Hashable] = set()
455:    all_coord_names: set[Hashable] = set()
456:    data_vars: set[Hashable] = set()  # list of data_vars
457:    dim_coords: dict[Hashable, Variable] = {}  # maps dim name to variable
458:    dims_sizes: dict[Hashable, int] = {}  # shared dimension sizes to expand variables
459:    variables_order: dict[Hashable, Variable] = {}  # variables in order of appearance
460:
461:    for ds in datasets:
462:        dims_sizes.update(ds.sizes)
463:        all_coord_names.update(ds.coords)
464:        data_vars.update(ds.data_vars)
465:        variables_order.update(ds.variables)
466:
467:        # preserves ordering of dimensions
468:        for dim in ds.dims:
469:            if dim in dims:
